results.title: Kong Volcano Agent Cloud: Self-Healing Claim Checked | explainx.ai Blog
results.content:
- Observability gap. None of the eight services in the release provides production observability, and Kong's advanced AI observability product was not generally available.
- Governance maturity. Futurum asks whether Kong's Token Vault, AI Cost Management and Advanced AI Observability become generally available.
- Approvals. Futurum cites its own survey finding 32% of organizations have human approval gates for irreversible agent actions. Kong has not said whether approvals are on by default.
- Neutrality. The article's title says Kong now hosts the agents it governs, which sits uneasily with Konnect's pitch as a neutral governance layer across clouds.
- Unknowns. Hosting location, pricing, open interfaces for workflows and queues, and whether traces export in OpenTelemetry format. [...] Kong wants to host the agents it already governs. Kong Volcano, announced September 30, 2026 and now being pushed again with a feature called LavaFlow, is an "agent cloud": a single platform where a coding agent can create a database, add sign-in, run durable workflows and deploy an app. Kong's pitch for LavaFlow is that it makes applications and agents self-healing. The product is real and installable. The self-healing claim has no published method behind it yet.

This post separates what Kong documents from what it claims, and lists what to check before building on it.

## TL;DR: Volcano in one table [...] Is it safe to let an agent deploy to it? That depends on what you grant the agent. Volcano offers approvals that pause a run until a person signs off, but Kong has not said whether they are on by default. Turn them on for deletes, schema changes and anything that touches user data.

Is the new Volcano the same as the 2025 Volcano SDK? No. Kong says they are separate products, and some write-ups mix them up.

## How to verify before you adopt

1. Install the CLI in a throwaway project and run the webhook recipe.
2. Kill a worker mid-workflow and confirm it resumes from the last checkpoint.
3. Branch the database and confirm the branch is isolated.
4. Ask Kong for pricing, hosting region and an export path in writing.
5. Check whether traces can reach your existing observability tools.

results.title: Christopher on Facebook: "Just saw Kong drop Volcano yesterday, and it's aimed at people building AI agents, not just chatting…"
results.content:
Why it matters here: a lot of Malaysian indie builders and SMEs can spin up a small agent-backed app (booking bot, support helper, internal ops tool) without stitching a dozen cloud pieces together first. Less infra yak-shaving, more "does this actually help my customer."

How I'd try it this week: pick one boring workflow you keep doing by hand (lead follow-up, invoice reminder, FAQ triage). Point your coding agent at Volcano, keep v1 tiny, and see if the agent can stay alive with real storage and auth instead of dying when you close the tab. If it sticks for a day without babysitting, you've got something worth showing a client.

[Image: May be a doodle of text] [...] # Christopher on Facebook: "Just saw Kong drop Volcano yesterday, and it's aimed at people building AI agents, not just chatting…"

Just saw Kong drop Volcano yesterday, and it's aimed at people building AI agents, not just chatting with them.

They packed durable compute, branchable Postgres, file storage, auth, and realtime into one platform so your agent has a real home instead of five half-wired services. It plugs into tools a lot of us already use (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex). There's a free Hobby tier, and the CLI is on npm.
